derivation: Both endpoints are measured against the TARGET test tree, because the verifier replaces t/ wholesale: required_to_pass is the nodes that fail or are absent with base-revision source under that tree and pass with target-revision source. must_keep_passing is exactly the nodes that pass at the no-op. excluded holds pre-existing failures, skips, the two cloud-backend modules that cannot run offline, and 107 nodes that are COLLECTION COLLATERAL: t/unit/backends/test_base.py cannot import at the no-op because two private names it imports do not yet exist, so every node in that module reads as absent. Counting them as required would have put 70.2 percent of the deterministic channel behind two stub definitions. They were separated by measurement, with a probe tree that restores collection using non-functional stubs: nodes that pass under that probe never needed the release and are excluded, nodes that still fail are required. All three sets are mutually disjoint.
